title: Humans on the Moon
objective: After this level you can describe the Apollo Moon landings and what they brought back.
summary: Apollo 11 landed on July 20, 1969. Twelve astronauts walked on the Moon by 1972 and brought back 382 kg of samples.

cards.headline: Only twelve people have ever walked on another world.
One small step
cards.body: On July 20, 1969, Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first people to walk on the Moon. Between 1969 and 1972, six Apollo landings put twelve astronauts on its surface.

cards.headline: Bringing the Moon home
cards.body: The Apollo astronauts brought back 382 kg of Moon rocks and soil. Scientists are still studying them, and they’re among the best evidence for how the Moon formed.

cards.fact: The last Moonwalkers left in December 1972.
cards.context: Their footprints are still up there. With no wind or rain on the Moon, nothing wears them away.

cards.headline: Moonwalk: recorded
learned: Twelve astronauts walked on the Moon by 1972
They brought back 382 kg of samples

questions.prompt: Who were the first two people to walk on the Moon?

options.label: Yuri Gagarin and Valentina Tereshkova
options.rationale: They were early spaceflight pioneers but never went to the Moon.

options.label: John Glenn and Alan Shepard
options.rationale: They flew early US missions, not Moon landings.

options.label: Galileo and Kepler
options.rationale: They studied the sky centuries earlier.

questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon during Apollo 11 on July 20, 1969.

questions.prompt: Why are the Apollo samples still valuable today?

options.label: They are the only rocks from space on Earth
options.rationale: Meteorites from space fall to Earth too.

options.label: They prove the Moon is made of cheese
They were used to fuel later rockets
Scientists keep studying them to learn how the Moon formed

questions.explanation: The 382 kg of Apollo samples keep yielding new evidence, including about how the Moon formed.

questions.prompt: From Level 18: what did Apollo samples reveal about where the Moon came from?

options.label: The Moon is made of the same rock as Mars
options.rationale: The match is with Earth, not Mars.

options.label: The Moon is older than the solar system
options.rationale: It formed about 4.5 billion years ago.

options.label: Moon rocks are chemically very similar to Earth’s mantle
The Moon was captured from the asteroid belt

questions.explanation: Apollo rocks closely match Earth’s mantle, supporting the idea that the Moon formed from debris of a giant impact.
